source_label: Private Codex task record, frozen newline-terminated prefix

events.heading: Initial audit package and theorem-level objection
events.edited_text: The task began from a packet-level review that verified 22 exact matrix and lattice checks but rejected certification of the global theorem. The stated obstruction was the simultaneous claim that X is diffeomorphic to S6 with c3(X)=2 and that a(X)=1, apparently contradicting the published CDP20 conclusion. The supplied modular assembler was also missing its ten packet inputs, so only packet 06 could initially be audited. The requested next step was to integrate the material, check the TeX, and conduct a literal model-to-model mathematical peer review.

events.heading: Complete source recovered; first integrated review
events.edited_text: The complete archive supplied all ten missing packets and removed the source-completeness objection. The integrated review confirmed three repairable local defects and the exact arithmetic, while treating the geometric attaching maps, integral specialization lattices, and Leray transgressions as not yet independently certified. It also identified a credible conductor-torsion gap in the published CDP argument, so CDP20 alone was no longer regarded as a decisive rejection argument.

events.heading: Independent full-manuscript review supplied
events.edited_text: A first independent full-manuscript review was supplied, with a second independent review expected separately. The project therefore preserved the independent review records rather than silently replacing them with the later reconstruction.

events.heading: Program renamed validate, repair, or disprove
events.edited_text: The user directed that the mathematical program be called validate/repair/disprove and that the record prioritize proofs, calculations, and counterexamples over verdict language. Here disproof was to mean determining exactly what fails and why, not merely producing a bare contradiction.

events.heading: Literature-first proof reconstruction begins
events.edited_text: The workbench adopted a proof-first and literature-first protocol: every literature-dependent step was checked against primary sources, and mathematical conclusions were to be recorded with exact theorem and page evidence rather than left as conversational notes.

events.heading: Intrinsic integral Leray route identified
events.edited_text: An intrinsic nearby-cycle and Leray route was isolated that did not assume the disputed cellular collapse. After integral specialization at the cusp, the three transgressions for p=-1 were shown to be multiplication by units, giving H1(X;Z)=H2(X;Z)=H3(X;Z)=0 once the full derivation was completed.

events.heading: Exact checks pass; two proof-layer transcription defects repaired
events.edited_text: The full-manuscript and independent core exact harnesses passed 28 of 28 and 38 of 38 assertions. The proof audit nevertheless found two mathematical transcription defects in the reconstruction layer: a missing modular-form factor in the period-frame argument and a false simplification in the Neron-Severi independence calculation. Both were repaired before geometric conclusions were promoted.

events.heading: Reviewer B becomes provisionally favorable
events.edited_text: Reviewer B's independent checkpoint became provisionally favorable on the reconstruction available at that time. The later workbench separately closed additional construction, cusp-specialization, algebraic-reduction, and based fundamental-group steps, without retroactively attributing those later proofs to Reviewer B.

events.heading: Topology, sphere recognition, and Picard branch reconstructed
events.edited_text: Complete derivations were written for the intrinsic specialization maps, based van Kampen presentation, integral cohomology, sphere recognition, and the Picard and algebraic-reduction branch. The topology and Picard conclusions ceased to be conditional within the workbench. At this checkpoint the printed Mayer-Vietoris identification remained an optional open route, while the candidate-specific conductor and base-change analysis refuted the relevant printed CDP inference.

events.heading: Candidate-specific independent validation supplied
events.edited_text: A further candidate-specific Reviewer B validation package was supplied for integration. Its report checked the global gluing, the period specialization, the algebraic-dimension construction, and the proposed CDP obstruction against selected source excerpts and exact identities.

events.heading: Independent Mayer-Vietoris topology certificate closed
events.edited_text: The alternate topological certificate was completed: the actual two-stage Mayer-Vietoris maps are primitive and unimodular for p=-1, and their dual obstruction maps agree with the three integral Leray d2 maps. This gave a second, independent integral calculation of the sphere topology.

events.heading: Hodge scalar dispute resolved
events.edited_text: Three checks agreed that the apparent h^(1,2)=2 computation divided by a vanishing derivative and thereby introduced a pole. The invariant-frame calculation instead gives h^(1,2)=1 and h^(1,1)=2. The corrected values were propagated through the proof, summaries, status tables, and machine ledgers.

events.heading: Bott-Chern and Aeppli dimensions determined
events.edited_text: Specialization of the published compact-threefold formulas gives h_BC^(1,2)=1, and the remaining duality and defect identities determine the complete Bott-Chern and Aeppli diamonds. The workbench records the formulas and their proof rather than only the resulting dimensions.

events.heading: Bott-Chern proof direction corrected
events.edited_text: A literature check found an exposition error in the Bott-Chern argument: the inequality k^(p,q)<=b_(p+q) follows from a surjection from the de Rham image onto K^(p,q), not from an injection of K^(p,q) into de Rham cohomology. Correcting the arrow left k^(2,0)=0 and all displayed Bott-Chern and Aeppli dimensions unchanged.

events.heading: Cusp Picard obstruction localized
events.edited_text: Once the smooth-fibre Appell-Humbert class vanishes, its restriction to the normalization of the cusp fibre is trivial by both injective cusp specialization and a direct toric support-function calculation. This localized the remaining problem to the global order-three and order-four logarithmic translations and their common twelve-fold winding.

events.heading: Local Hodge and cusp repairs isolated
events.edited_text: Independent audits preserved h^(1,2)=1 but required three local repairs: restoration of an omitted frame unit, stating cusp matrices modulo the degeneration parameter, and writing the evaluation splitting explicitly. The manuscript's separate cusp-torsion assertion was recorded as refuted rather than folded into those repairs.

events.heading: Integral topology and analytic invariants assembled
events.edited_text: For (l0,l1,l2)=(0,1,-1), the affine drift vanishes and p=-1. Primitive cusp specialization and the three explicit Leray transgressions give H1=H2=H3=0, while the based presentation <c,x,y | c central, xy=1, x^3=c, y^4=c^(-1)> is trivial. The independent collapse calculation agrees, giving X diffeomorphic to S6 and c3(X)=2. The Appell-Humbert and Picard calculation gives a(X)=1 and a line bundle non-torsion on every fibre; conductor duality and base change produce the candidate-specific failure of the printed CDP route. Direct-image calculations give h^(1,2)=1 and h^(1,1)=2.

events.heading: Purely analytic Picard route formulated
events.edited_text: A third Picard route was formulated directly in Appell-Humbert terms. The key step was to decompose every equivariant boundary class into a toric support-function component and a logarithmic-unit component with zero Chern class, rather than infer the result by analogy with the topological certificate.

events.heading: Third Picard certificate completed and propagated
events.edited_text: The analytic all-Picard proof passed adversarial review. Stale statements describing only two certificates were replaced by the actual cocycle, norm, cusp-winding, and toric support-function argument, and the proof was propagated through the global status surfaces.

events.heading: Formal typing and formula directions repaired
events.edited_text: A final proof audit found and repaired a formal typing gap in the analytic Picard argument and two smaller formula-direction errors in the candidate construction. The corrected formulas were propagated into the proof, status, overview, and audit layers before publication QA.

events.heading: A peer-verification publication requested
events.edited_text: The user requested that the completed work be published as a serious peer-verification record: more extensive than an ordinary referee report, reproducible at theorem level, and useful for eventual human specialist checking.

events.heading: Publication category fixed
events.edited_text: The resulting genre was fixed as a reproducible theorem-by-theorem peer-verification monograph, not a conventional referee report. A DOI release was made contingent on mathematical coherence, citations, reproducibility artifacts, and release QA rather than on a verdict alone.

events.heading: Internal dependency closure audited
events.edited_text: The live ledgers contained no unresolved internal premise. Their only OPEN mathematical rows concerned independent specialist replication and external adjudication; the topology, Hodge, Picard, and corrected-CDP chains were VERIFIED internally with complete proofs recorded in the workbench.

events.heading: Visual QA catches a literal TeX artifact
events.edited_text: The publication visual pass caught bare qquad tokens printed as text in abstract separators. Every occurrence was repaired, demonstrating why rendered-page inspection remained a release gate even after clean compilation and structural PDF checks.

events.heading: Global and relative CDP nonvanishing separated
events.edited_text: The final status audit corrected a logical conflation. Vanishing of R2 f_*(T_X tensor L) is a stronger relative condition that supplies a global H2 vanishing only after suitable twisting; it is not equivalent to global H2(X,T_X tensor L)=0. The candidate's relative nonvanishing follows from conductor and base-change arguments, while global nonvanishing for every line bundle follows separately by contraposing the corrected theorem against c3(X)=2. No theorem status changed.

events.heading: Publication provenance frozen without publishing the private session
events.edited_text: A byte-exact newline-terminated prefix of the private task record was frozen and hashed. The public chronology retains selected source ordinals and event hashes while excluding raw conversation, local paths, private links, tool traffic, and credentials. This makes the release derivation auditable to an authorized holder of the private source without turning the private session itself into the publication.

status_at_boundary: At the edition boundary the claim ledger records 42 VERIFIED, zero CONDITIONAL, two OPEN, and four REFUTED claims; the uncertainty ledger records 12 VERIFIED, three OPEN, and three REFUTED items; and all 26 morphism records are VERIFIED. The OPEN mathematical rows concern independent specialist replication and external adjudication, not missing internal premises. Attribution and model provenance are recorded separately from theorem status.
